task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Northrill's decision to divide its snow-clearing work between two contractors. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Northrill Council awarded its next winter snow-clearance work through two contracts instead of the previous combined contract.
The road-clearing contract is $188,000 and the pedestrian-route contract is $124,000, for a combined base price of $312,000.
The previous season's combined base contract was $290,000, a different figure from the amount ultimately paid for all weather-related callouts.
The new base prices cover standby capacity and specified routine deployments, with exceptional additional work billed under separate agreed rates.
The road contractor will handle the priority vehicle network, while the second contractor will clear designated footways and public-building approaches.
The pedestrian route list includes school approaches, the civic center and the main bus interchange rather than every sidewalk in the city.
The former combined contractor did not submit a bid this year, and the council has not described the change as a dismissal for misconduct.
Operations manager Elen Marr said, "A cleared road with an uncleared crossing can still leave someone unable to finish the journey."
The council will assign one city duty officer to coordinate deployment and resolve gaps where road and footway responsibilities meet.
Both contractors must report completed sections to that officer, rather than assuming the other contractor has dealt with connecting crossings.
A mobility group asked for crossing points and bus-stop approaches to appear explicitly on the pedestrian route maps.
Mobility group representative Pera Voss said, "The last few yards are not a small detail when they are the yards you cannot get through."
The final pedestrian route maps will be published before the contracts begin on Nov. 1, 2026.
The contracts run through March 31, 2027, with any extension subject to the supplied approval process.
The council has not promised that every listed route will be clear by the same hour after every snowfall.
Deployment order depends on the conditions reported to the duty officer and the priority network described in the contracts.
The city's own crews will continue maintaining grit bins and handling smaller tasks outside the contractors' main routes.
The approved award report contains no forecast of how many major snow events the coming season will bring.
A public contact line will accept reports of blocked designated routes, but reports will enter the coordinated work queue rather than guarantee an immediate visit.
The depot will hold a joint route familiarization session for the two contractors before winter operations begin.
The council will compare completed work records and public reports at a midseason review.
The depot still uses a large wall map with removable route markers alongside its newer dispatch screens.

forbidden_additions: A final all-inclusive winter cost or a forecast of snowfall.
The previous contractor fired for misconduct.
Guaranteed immediate clearance of all streets or sidewalks.
preserve: The split responsibilities and the need to coordinate connecting routes.
Base prices distinguished from weather-dependent additional work.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
